title: By Time
tag: Three verses that judge how a life is spent.
hadith: There are two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6412
opening: Allah swears by time itself. Not by gold, not by kingdoms, but by the hours that slip past us every day. Imam al-Shafi'i said that if people reflected on this surah alone, it would be enough for them, a remark Ibn Kathir records at the start of his tafsir. Three short verses, and they hold the whole map of a successful life.
verse: The oath is by al-'Asr: time, the age, or the late afternoon, when the day is ending and its work is weighed. The verdict follows: every human being is in loss. Ibn Kathir explains that this is the default. Loss is not something you fall into; it is where you already stand unless you climb out. Then comes the exception, with four conditions. Faith, which sets the direction. Righteous action, which turns faith into deeds. Urging one another to the truth, which means you cannot succeed alone. And urging one another to patience, because truth will cost you something. Notice that two of the four are about other people. A private, comfortable faith that never helps anyone else does not meet the standard of this surah.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim wrote in al-Fawa'id that wasting time is worse than death, because death cuts you off from this world, while wasted time cuts you off from Allah and the Hereafter. He also described a ladder in this surah: first you know the truth, then you act on it, then you teach it, and then you stay patient through all three. Hasan al-Basri put it more personally: O son of Adam, you are nothing but days, and whenever a day passes, a part of you has gone.
modern: Seneca, the Roman philosopher, wrote that it is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it. Peter Drucker, the father of modern management, told executives that time is the scarcest resource, and unless it is managed nothing else can be. Both of them saw time as an asset. The surah goes further. Time is not only an asset you own. It is a trust you will answer for.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Komai nisan jifa, ƙasa zai faɗo»: however far a stone is thrown, it will fall back to the ground. Every day you spend will land somewhere, and you will meet it again.
practices: Each night, ask four questions: Did I strengthen my faith today? What good did I actually do? Whom did I urge towards the truth? Where did I hold firm with patience?
Protect one block of focused time each morning before messages and meetings.
Choose one person this week to encourage in something good, gently and in private.
reflect: Which hour of my day is most often lost, and to what?
Who in my life urges me to the truth, and whom do I urge?
closing: Time is passing whether you use it or not. Al-'Asr does not ask you to do everything. It asks you to make sure that each day carries faith, action, truth and patience. Begin with today.

verses.ar: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
verses.en: By time,

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
verses.en: Indeed, mankind is in loss,

verses.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
verses.en: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.

title: The One
tag: Fifteen words that answer the oldest question: who is God?
hadith: By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an.
Sahih al-Bukhari 5013
opening: Some people came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: describe your Lord to us. The answer came in four short verses. Ibn Kathir reports that this was the occasion of its revelation, and the Prophet said it is equal to a third of the Qur'an, because the Qur'an speaks of three things: rulings, stories, and who Allah is. This surah is the purest statement of the third.
verse: Say: He is Allah, Ahad, One. Not one of a kind, but One with no second, no partner and no division. Allah, al-Samad. Ibn Abbas explained al-Samad as the Master who is perfect in His sovereignty, His knowledge and His wisdom, the One to whom all creation turns in need, while He needs no one. He neither begets nor is born, which rejects every idea of a god with a family or a beginning. And there is none comparable to Him. Every verse removes a false picture of God, until only the true one is left.
scholars: Ibn Taymiyyah wrote an entire book on this surah alone. He showed that it holds the two halves of tawhid: what we affirm of Allah, His oneness and perfection, and what we deny of Him, any partner, child or equal. The scholars explain that it is called al-Ikhlas, sincerity, because whoever truly believes it purifies his worship of everyone else. Belief in al-Samad means your needs go first to Allah, not to people.
modern: The American writer David Foster Wallace told a graduating class in 2005 that there is no such thing as not worshipping. Everybody worships something. If you worship money and things, he said, you will never feel you have enough. Today few people carve idols, but many hearts bow to salary, status, approval or a title. Al-Ikhlas is the cure. When Allah alone is al-Samad, nothing else can own you.
nigerian: In Hausaland people say «Allah ɗaya, gari bamban»: God is One, though the towns differ. Our customs, tribes and languages vary, but the One we turn to is the same.
practices: Recite al-Ikhlas three times morning and evening, slowly, thinking about one name each time.
Before a request to a person, ask Allah first for the same thing.
Notice one thing this week your heart leans on too much, and name it honestly.
reflect: Where do I turn first when I am in need?
What do I fear losing so much that it has started to rule me?
closing: Allah is One, He is al-Samad, and nothing is like Him. Every time you recite these words, you are freeing your heart from every other master.

verses.ar: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
verses.en: Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,

verses.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
verses.en: Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.

verses.ar: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
verses.en: He neither begets nor is born,

verses.ar: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ
verses.en: Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

title: The Cave
tag: Four stories, four trials: faith, wealth, knowledge and power.
hadith: Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal.
Sahih Muslim 809
opening: Ibn Kathir reports that the Quraysh, guided by the rabbis of Madinah, tested the Prophet with questions about young men who disappeared long ago, a great traveller, and the soul. Surah al-Kahf was the answer. Many scholars read it as four stories that map the four great trials of life.
verse: The first is the trial of faith: the young men of the cave who left everything rather than give up their belief, and who prayed, our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly. The second is the trial of wealth: the man with two gardens who forgot who gave them to him. Allah tells us that wealth and children are the adornment of this life, but lasting good deeds are better. The third is the trial of knowledge: Musa, a great prophet, travelling to learn from al-Khidr, and learning that there is always wisdom beyond what we can see. The fourth is the trial of power: Dhul-Qarnayn, who ruled the earth and still said, this is a mercy from my Lord. The surah closes with the cure for all four: do righteous deeds, and associate no one in the worship of your Lord.
scholars: Ibn Kathir draws out from the story of Musa and al-Khidr that a seeker of knowledge must be humble and patient, even when he is already learned. Ibn al-Qayyim taught that the garden owner's mistake began in his heart before it showed on his tongue: he saw the blessing and forgot the Giver. The companion 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, one of the wealthiest of them, said: we were tested with hardship and we were patient, then we were tested with ease and we were not patient. That is the garden owner's trial in one sentence.
modern: Plato records Socrates saying that he was wise only in knowing that he did not know. Musa's journey teaches the same lesson, but with a direction: humility before Allah's greater wisdom. Modern leadership writers like Jim Collins found that the most effective leaders combine strong will with real personal humility. Dhul-Qarnayn is that leader, a thousand years before the business books.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Duniya mace da ciki ce»: the world is a pregnant woman, and no one knows what she will give birth to. Like Musa watching al-Khidr, we often judge events before their meaning is born.
practices: Read Surah al-Kahf on Friday, even a portion, and choose one of the four trials to reflect on.
When a blessing arrives, say «Ma sha' Allah, la quwwata illa billah», as the garden owner should have.
Before judging a hard event, wait and ask: what might I not yet be seeing?
reflect: Which of the four trials am I facing most right now?
Where has a blessing made me forget the One who gave it?
closing: Faith, wealth, knowledge and power will all test you. Al-Kahf gives you one shelter for every storm: sincere deeds, done for Allah alone.

verses.ar: إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
verses.en: [Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."

verses.ar: ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا
verses.en: Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope.

verses.ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَٰلِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدًۢا
verses.en: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."

title: Rise at Night
tag: How the night prepares you for the weight of the day.
hadith: The best prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer at night.
Sahih Muslim 1163
opening: O you wrapped in garments. This surah came early in Makkah, when the Prophet, peace be upon him, was about to carry the heaviest message ever given to a human being. Before the burden, Allah gave him a training programme: stand at night.
verse: Arise at night, except a little: half of it, or a little less or more, and recite the Qur'an with tartil, measured and clear. Then the reason: We will cast upon you a heavy word. The night is the preparation for the weight. Allah says that rising at night is firmer in its effect and clearer in its words. The final verse came later, and it lightens the duty with mercy. Allah knows some of you will be ill, some will travel seeking His bounty, and some will strive in His cause, so recite what is easy. Establish prayer, give zakah, lend Allah a goodly loan, and seek His forgiveness.
scholars: Ibn Kathir cites the narration of 'A'ishah in Sahih Muslim that night prayer was obligatory on the Prophet and his companions for a year, until Allah sent down the lightening at the end of this surah. Ibn Abbas explained the rising of the night as standing after sleep. Ibn al-Qayyim described the night as the time when the heart is free from the noise of people, so the tongue and the heart agree in what they say.
modern: Cal Newport, in his book Deep Work, argues that the most valuable work happens in long, undisturbed blocks of attention. Many leaders protect the early morning for exactly this reason. Al-Muzzammil teaches that the deepest work of all is with your Lord, and that it makes you stronger for every other kind.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Sannu sannu bai hana zuwa»: slowly, slowly does not stop you from arriving. Tartil, the measured recitation, is the same spirit. A little, done steadily, carries you further than a burst that fades.
practices: Pray two rak'ahs before Fajr, even if only for ten minutes, and recite slowly.
Keep the first minutes after waking free from your phone.
End each night with istighfar, as the surah itself ends.
reflect: What 'heavy word' am I carrying in this season of life?
What small, steady night habit can I keep even when travelling?
closing: The weight of your responsibilities will not get lighter. But the night can make you stronger. Stand a little, recite slowly, and ask forgiveness. That is how the Prophet was prepared.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ
verses.en: O you who wraps himself [in clothing],

verses.ar: قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
verses.en: Arise [to pray] the night, except for a little -

verses.ar: نِّصْفَهُۥٓ أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
verses.en: Half of it - or subtract from it a little

verses.ar: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
verses.en: Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation.

verses.ar: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا
verses.en: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.

verses.ar: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيْلِ هِىَ أَشَدُّ وَطْـًٔا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا
verses.en: Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence [of heart and tongue] and more suitable for words.

verses.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ وَطَآئِفَةٌ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَ وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرْضَىٰ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌۢ
verses.en: Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muḥammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allāh determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur’ān. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allāh and others fighting for the cause of Allāh. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakāh and loan Allāh a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allāh. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

title: Discipline
tag: Small, steady deeds beat great intentions.
hadith: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are small.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6464, Sahih Muslim 783
opening: Everyone wants the result of discipline. Few want the daily cost. Islam calls this struggle mujahadat al-nafs, striving against the self, and it promises something remarkable to those who take it on.
verse: Allah says: as for those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways, and Allah is with those who do good. The striving comes first, and the guidance follows. You do not wait to feel motivated and then begin. You begin, and Allah opens the road. The Prophet, peace be upon him, added the method: the deeds Allah loves most are the consistent ones, even if they are small.
scholars: Imam al-Ghazali, in the Ihya, compares the soul to an untrained horse. You do not break it in a day. You train it gradually, holding it back from what harms it and leading it towards what is good, until good habits feel natural. Ibn al-Qayyim warned that the soul gives in to whatever it is allowed to repeat, so the real battle is not the single decision but the habit behind it.
modern: Will Durant, summarising Aristotle, wrote that we are what we repeatedly do, so excellence is not an act but a habit. James Clear puts it in modern terms in Atomic Habits: you do not rise to the level of your goals, you fall to the level of your systems. Both agree with the hadith. Small and consistent wins.
nigerian: The Yoruba say «Iṣẹ́ l'òògùn ìṣẹ́»: work is the medicine for poverty. There is no shortcut around steady effort, in this world or in the next.
practices: Choose one small deed and do it daily for forty days without missing.
Set a fixed time for it, tied to something you already do, such as after Fajr.
When you miss a day, restart the next day without guilt or drama.
reflect: Which good habit have I started many times but never kept?
What is one thing I keep repeating that is training my soul in the wrong direction?
closing: Strive, and Allah will guide. Keep it small, keep it steady, and let consistency do what bursts of effort never can.

verses.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُوا۟ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.en: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allāh is with the doers of good.

title: Patience
tag: Not passive waiting, but steadfast action under pressure.
hadith: How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of it is good. If something good happens he is grateful, and that is good for him. If something harmful befalls him he is patient, and that is good for him.
Sahih Muslim 2999
Patience is at the first strike of calamity.
Sahih al-Bukhari 1283, Sahih Muslim 926
opening: Patience is mentioned in the Qur'an more than ninety times, according to Imam Ahmad. It is not weakness, and it is not simply waiting. It is the strength to stay upright when everything pushes you to fall.
verse: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer; Allah is with the patient. Then Allah tells us the test is certain: fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits. And He gives good news to the patient, those who, when disaster strikes, say: to Allah we belong and to Him we return. Upon them are blessings and mercy from their Lord, and they are the rightly guided. Patience is paired with prayer, because you cannot hold steady on your own strength alone.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim, in 'Uddat al-Sabirin, divides patience into three: patience in obeying Allah, patience in staying away from what He forbids, and patience with what He decrees. He defines it as holding the soul back from panic, the tongue from complaint, and the limbs from acting wrongly. The Prophet's teaching that patience is at the first strike reminds us that the real test is in the first moment, not after the shock has passed.
modern: Viktor Frankl, who survived the Nazi camps, wrote that everything can be taken from a person except one thing: the freedom to choose one's attitude in any set of circumstances. Angela Duckworth's research on grit found that sustained perseverance predicts success better than talent. The Qur'an adds the anchor they lack: you are patient because you belong to Allah and are returning to Him.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Mai haƙuri yakan dafa dutse har ya sha romonsa»: the patient person can cook a stone until he drinks its broth. And they say «Haƙuri maganin duniya»: patience is the medicine of this world.
practices: When bad news arrives, say «Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un» before saying anything else.
Pray two rak'ahs when under pressure, as the verse instructs.
Delay any reply written in anger by at least one hour.
reflect: Which of the three kinds of patience is hardest for me right now?
How do I behave in the first moment of bad news?
closing: Every trial ends, but the reward of patience does not. Hold steady, pray, and remember: to Allah we belong, and to Him we return.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
verses.en: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allāh is with the patient.

verses.ar: وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىْءٍ مِّنَ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَٱلْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
verses.en: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient,

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
verses.en: Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allāh, and indeed to Him we will return."

verses.ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَٰتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُهْتَدُونَ
verses.en: Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.

title: Truthfulness
tag: Truth as a path, not a single act.
hadith: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man keeps telling the truth until he is recorded with Allah as truthful.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6094, Sahih Muslim 2607
opening: In a world of spin, half-truths and convenient silence, truthfulness can feel like a luxury. Islam treats it as a foundation. Before the Prophet, peace be upon him, received revelation, the people of Makkah already called him al-Sadiq al-Amin, the truthful and the trustworthy.
verse: O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful. And in Surah al-Ahzab: fear Allah and speak words that are straight and accurate. He will set right your deeds for you and forgive your sins. Notice the promise. Straight speech repairs your work. When your words are reliable, your decisions, relationships and reputation all become sound.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim described sidq as having three places: truth in words, truth in deeds, and truth in one's inner state, so that what is inside matches what is shown. The hadith describes truth as a path. Each honest sentence makes the next one easier, until truth becomes your nature and Allah records you as truthful. Lying works the same way in reverse.
modern: Stephen Covey taught that trust is built in small deposits and lost in large withdrawals, and that people judge us by our track record, not our intentions. In regulated work, where reports and disclosures carry legal weight, this is not only ethics. It is survival. An accurate report delivered late is worth more than a polished one that bends the facts.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Gaskiya ta fi kwabo»: truth is worth more than money. A coin can be spent once. A reputation for honesty keeps paying.
practices: Remove exaggeration from your speech this week, even in jokes and small claims.
When you make a mistake at work, report it early and plainly.
Before signing or sending anything, ask: is every sentence here true?
reflect: Where do I shade the truth to avoid discomfort?
Is my inner state the same as the face I show?
closing: Speak straight words, and Allah will set right your deeds. Walk the path of truth one sentence at a time.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَكُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
verses.en: O you who have believed, fear Allāh and be with those who are true.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا
verses.en: O you who have believed, fear Allāh and speak words of appropriate justice.

verses.ar: يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَٰلَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا
verses.en: He will [then] amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allāh and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.

title: Sincerity
tag: Being the same person in private and in public.
hadith: Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended.
Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907
opening: Imam al-Bukhari opened his entire collection with one hadith: actions are judged by intentions. The scholars said this single hadith is a third of knowledge, because every deed has an outward form and an inner reason, and Allah looks at both.
verse: They were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, upright, and to establish prayer and give zakah. That is the correct religion. Sincerity is not an extra. It is the condition that makes every other act count.
scholars: Ibn Ata'illah, in his Hikam, wrote: bury your existence in the earth of obscurity, for whatever sprouts without being buried does not flourish. A seed that wants to be seen never grows roots. The Prophet, peace be upon him, warned that hidden shirk creeps more quietly than an ant, in a narration recorded by Imam Ahmad, and al-Ghazali gave a whole book of the Ihya to the dangers of showing off. And Ibn al-Qayyim said that a deed without sincerity is like a traveller who fills his bag with sand: it weighs him down and does not benefit him.
modern: Psychologists distinguish between intrinsic motivation, doing something because it matters to you, and extrinsic motivation, doing it for reward or praise. Research consistently finds that intrinsic motivation lasts longer and produces better work. Islam goes a step further: the purest motive is the face of Allah, which no audience can give or take away.
nigerian: The Yoruba say «Ìwà l'ẹ̀sìn»: character is religion. What you are when no one is watching is the truest measure of your faith.
practices: Before any significant task, pause for three seconds and renew your intention.
Do one good deed this week that no one will ever know about.
When praised, quietly say «Alhamdulillah» and give the credit back to Allah.
reflect: Would I still do this if no one ever found out?
Whose approval am I most hungry for?
closing: Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but at your heart and your deeds. Purify the intention, and even small actions become great.

verses.ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓا۟ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ
verses.en: And they were not commanded except to worship Allāh, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakāh. And that is the correct religion.

title: Courage
tag: Your appointed time cannot be moved, so live boldly.
hadith: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in both there is good. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be helpless.
Sahih Muslim 2664
opening: Fear of death, fear of travel, fear of failure, fear of people. Much of what stops us is not danger itself but the fear of it. The Qur'an removes the root of that fear by settling one question: who decides when you die?
verse: No soul can die except by Allah's permission, at a term already written. And: wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built high and strong. If the appointed time is fixed, then cowardice does not lengthen your life, and courage does not shorten it. What fear really steals is not your years but the good you could have done in them.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim, in al-Wabil al-Sayyib, reports Ibn Taymiyyah saying: what can my enemies do to me? My paradise and my garden are in my heart. If they imprison me, it is seclusion; if they exile me, it is travel; if they kill me, it is martyrdom. The great general Khalid ibn al-Walid, who fought in battle after battle, is reported to have said on his deathbed that he was dying in his bed despite seeking death on the battlefield, so let the eyes of cowards never sleep.
modern: Seneca wrote that we suffer more often in imagination than in reality. Modern psychology agrees: avoidance makes fear grow, while gradual exposure shrinks it. Courage is not the absence of fear. It is action taken while afraid, with trust in Allah steadying the heart.
nigerian: Wole Soyinka wrote: the man dies in all who keep silent in the face of tyranny. For him, the death to fear was not the body's but the conscience's.
practices: Recite the travel du'a and Ayat al-Kursi before every journey, then travel with a settled heart.
Do one thing this week that fear has been delaying.
When anxious about the future, say «Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil».
reflect: What would I do differently if I truly believed my time is already written?
Where does fear silence me when I should speak?
closing: Your life is in Allah's hands, not your enemies', not the road's, and not chance's. Be the strong believer. Seek help from Allah, and do not be helpless.

verses.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبًا مُّؤَجَّلًا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِۦ مِنْهَا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِۦ مِنْهَا وَسَنَجْزِى ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
verses.en: And it is not [possible] for one to die except by permission of Allāh at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.

verses.ar: أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُوا۟ يُدْرِككُّمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنتُمْ فِى بُرُوجٍ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا۟ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا۟ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنْ عِندِكَ قُلْ كُلٌّ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلْقَوْمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ حَدِيثًا
verses.en: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. But if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allāh"; and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All [things] are from Allāh." So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?

title: Gratitude
tag: The surest way to keep a blessing is to thank its Giver.
hadith: Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah.
Sunan Abi Dawud 4811, Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1954
opening: Some blessings we notice only when they leave: health, safety, a parent's voice. Gratitude is the habit of noticing them while they are still here.
verse: And remember when your Lord proclaimed: if you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe. This is one of the clearest promises in the Qur'an. Gratitude is not just good manners. It is the law by which blessings grow.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim, in Madarij al-Salikin, taught that true gratitude has three parts: the heart acknowledges that the blessing is from Allah, the tongue praises Him for it, and the limbs use it in obeying Him. Wealth used in sin is not thanked, however often one says alhamdulillah. The Prophet linked thanking Allah with thanking people, because Allah's gifts usually reach us through human hands.
modern: Psychologist Robert Emmons found in his studies that people who regularly wrote down what they were grateful for reported better wellbeing, more optimism and even better sleep. Modern science is measuring what the Qur'an promised: gratitude increases what you have, beginning with your peace of mind.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Wanda bai gode wa kaɗan ba, ba zai gode wa da yawa ba»: whoever does not give thanks for a little will not give thanks for much.
practices: Each night, write three specific blessings from the day.
Thank one person this week in detail for something they did.
Use one blessing deliberately in obedience: your wealth in charity, your skill in service.
reflect: Which blessing have I stopped noticing?
Whose help do I take for granted?
closing: If you are grateful, Allah will increase you. Notice, praise and use well, and watch what grows.

verses.ar: وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِى لَشَدِيدٌ
verses.en: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'"

title: Renewal
tag: No door is closed while you are still breathing.
hadith: Every son of Adam makes mistakes, and the best of those who make mistakes are those who repent.
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2499, Sunan Ibn Majah 4251
opening: Many people carry their past like a weight they cannot put down. A failure, a habit, a word they wish they had never said. Islam does not ask you to pretend it never happened. It offers you something better: a real way back.
verse: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Ibn Kathir notes that this verse is addressed to every sinner, and that no sin is too great for repentance. Allah calls them My servants even while describing their wrongdoing. The relationship is not broken.
scholars: The scholars give three conditions for repentance between a person and Allah: stop the sin, regret it, and resolve not to return. If it involves another person's right, a fourth is added: restore that right. Ibn al-Qayyim made a striking observation: a sin that leaves a person humble and broken before Allah can be better for him than a good deed that leaves him proud.
modern: Carol Dweck's research on the growth mindset shows that people who see failure as something to learn from recover and improve, while those who see it as proof of who they are get stuck. Tawbah is the deepest form of this: your mistake is not your identity, and your Lord is waiting for your return.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Komai nisan dare, gari zai waye»: however long the night, the dawn will come.
practices: Say «Astaghfirullah wa atubu ilayh» one hundred times a day, as the Prophet did.
Choose one habit to leave this month, and replace it with a good one.
If you owe someone an apology or a debt, settle it this week.
reflect: What am I still carrying that I have never truly repented from?
Whose right do I need to restore?
closing: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Turn back today. The door is open.

verses.ar: قُلْ يَٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.en: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

title: Wise at Work
tag: Strong and trustworthy: the Qur'an's job description.
hadith: A believer is not stung from the same hole twice.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6133, Sahih Muslim 2998
opening: Some people are honest but naive. Others are clever but cannot be trusted. The Qur'an asks for both qualities together, and it gives us two prophets as models: Musa and Yusuf.
verse: One of the daughters of the old man of Madyan said: O my father, hire him; the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy. Strength is competence, the ability to do the job. Trustworthiness is integrity, the reliability to do it right. And Yusuf, after years in prison, said to the king: appoint me over the storehouses of the land; I am a knowing guardian. He named his qualifications plainly: knowledge and the ability to protect.
scholars: Ibn Kathir explains that Yusuf asked for this post because he knew his own ability and the benefit it would bring to the people, and that it is permissible to seek a role when one is qualified and fears it would otherwise be lost. Ibn Taymiyyah, in al-Siyasah al-Shar'iyyah, built a theory of appointment on these two qualities, strength and trust, noting that they rarely come together perfectly, so the leader must weigh which one a role needs most. The hadith adds shrewdness: a believer learns from being stung once and does not walk into the same trap again.
modern: Adam Grant, in Give and Take, found that the most successful people at work are often generous givers, but only when they are also wise about protecting themselves from those who take advantage. That is the strong and trustworthy believer: generous, honest, and not naive.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Ɗan hakin da ka raina, shi ke tsone maka ido»: the little blade of grass you look down on is the one that pokes your eye. At work, small risks ignored become large problems.
practices: List the two or three skills your role most needs, and grow one of them this quarter.
Keep written records of key decisions and agreements.
After any setback, write down the lesson so you are not stung twice.
reflect: Am I stronger in competence or in trustworthiness, and how do I grow the weaker one?
Which small risk am I currently ignoring?
closing: Be strong and trustworthy. Know your craft, guard your integrity, and learn from every sting.

verses.ar: قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
verses.en: One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."

verses.ar: قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلْأَرْضِ إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ
verses.en: [Joseph] said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."

title: Serving with Counsel
tag: Loyalty that tells the truth.
hadith: The religion is sincere counsel. We asked: to whom? He said: to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.
Sahih Muslim 55
opening: Many of us spend our working lives close to a principal, a chairman or a chief executive. That closeness is a trust. It can make you a flatterer, a silent observer, or a true adviser. Islam asks you to be the third.
verse: Musa, a prophet of great rank, said to al-Khidr: may I follow you, so that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught? And he promised: you will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. Here is the posture of a good student and a good subordinate: humility, patience and commitment. Yet even Musa spoke up when he saw something that seemed wrong. Respect and honest questions are not opposites.
scholars: Ibn Rajab, in Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam, explains that sincere counsel to leaders means helping them in what is right, obeying them in it, reminding them gently and kindly when they err, and not flattering them. The scholars advised that correction of a leader should be done privately where possible, protecting his dignity while still delivering the truth.
modern: Kim Scott, in Radical Candor, describes the best working relationships as caring personally while challenging directly. Care without challenge becomes flattery. Challenge without care becomes aggression. Nasihah is both together: I tell you the truth because I want you to succeed.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Idan kunne ya ji, jiki ya tsira»: when the ear listens, the body is safe. A wise principal listens to sincere counsel, and a wise adviser delivers it in a way that can be heard.
practices: Raise concerns privately, with facts and a proposed solution.
Separate your loyalty to the person from your loyalty to the truth, and keep both.
Make du'a for your principal's guidance and success.
reflect: When did I last stay silent when I should have advised?
Do I deliver hard truths in a way that can be heard?
closing: Serve with patience like Musa, and speak with sincerity as the Prophet taught. Real loyalty tells the truth, kindly.

verses.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا
verses.en: Moses said to him, "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?"

verses.ar: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًا
verses.en: [Moses] said, "You will find me, if Allāh wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in [any] order."

title: Leadership as Trust
tag: Every role is a flock you will answer for.
hadith: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.
Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829
opening: In Islam, leadership is not a prize. It is a trust, an amanah, and the higher the position, the heavier the questioning on the Day of Judgement. Whether you lead a company, a department or a household, you are a shepherd.
verse: Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. And to the Prophet himself, Allah said: it is by mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them; had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. Then, when you have decided, rely upon Allah. Justice, gentleness, consultation, decision and trust: that is a complete leadership model in two verses.
scholars: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account. As caliph, he is reported to have said that if a mule stumbled on a road in Iraq, he feared Allah would ask him why he had not levelled the path. Ibn Taymiyyah wrote that giving positions to the most qualified, not to relatives or friends, is part of rendering trusts to whom they are due.
modern: Jim Collins, in Good to Great, found that the leaders of the most successful companies combined deep personal humility with fierce professional will. Robert Greenleaf called this servant leadership: the leader exists to serve the people he leads. The shepherd hadith said it fourteen centuries earlier.
nigerian: Chinua Achebe wrote that the trouble with Nigeria is simply and squarely a failure of leadership. And a maxim that Shehu Usman dan Fodio often cited holds that a kingdom can endure with unbelief, but it cannot endure with injustice.
practices: Before a major decision, consult the people it affects.
Review one appointment or delegation: is it based on competence and trust?
Hold a weekly self-account: whom did I serve, and whom did I neglect?
reflect: Who is in my flock, at work and at home?
Do the people I lead feel my gentleness or my harshness?
closing: You are a shepherd, and you will be asked about your flock. Lead with justice, consult with humility, decide with courage, and rely on Allah.

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا۟ ٱلْأَمَٰنَٰتِ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ أَن تَحْكُمُوا۟ بِٱلْعَدْلِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًۢا بَصِيرًا
verses.en: Indeed, Allāh commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allāh instructs you. Indeed, Allāh is ever Hearing and Seeing.

verses.ar: فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لَٱنفَضُّوا۟ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
verses.en: So by mercy from Allāh, [O Muḥammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allāh. Indeed, Allāh loves those who rely [upon Him].

title: The Power of Speech
tag: Musa's prayer for a clear tongue, and how to speak well.
hadith: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47
opening: Before Musa faced Pharaoh, the most powerful man on earth, he did not ask for an army. He asked for a clear tongue. Words would be his weapon, and he knew it.
verse: He said: my Lord, expand for me my chest, ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, so they may understand my speech. Notice the order. First a calm, open heart. Then an easier task. Then clear speech. And the purpose: that they may understand. Good speech is not about sounding impressive. It is about being understood.
scholars: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib is reported to have said: a person is hidden beneath his tongue; speak, and you will be known. Imam al-Nawawi, commenting on the hadith of speaking good or staying silent, wrote that a person should not speak unless the benefit of speaking is clear, and if in doubt, silence is better.
modern: Aristotle taught in his Rhetoric that persuasion rests on three things: ethos, the speaker's character; pathos, the listener's emotions; and logos, the logic of the argument. Stephen Covey added: seek first to understand, then to be understood. The best speakers listen first, then speak briefly, clearly and with the main point up front.
nigerian: Chinua Achebe wrote in Things Fall Apart that among the Igbo the art of conversation is highly regarded, and proverbs are the palm-oil with which words are eaten. A well-chosen image makes a hard point easy to swallow.
practices: Recite Musa's du'a before every important meeting or presentation.
Start with your main point in one sentence, then give the reasons.
Replace filler words with a short, deliberate pause.
reflect: Do people understand me the first time, or do I need to repeat myself?
When did my words last cause harm I could have avoided?
closing: My Lord, expand my chest, ease my task, and untie the knot from my tongue. Speak good, or stay silent, and let every word be understood.

verses.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
verses.en: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]

verses.ar: وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
verses.en: And ease for me my task

verses.ar: وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى
verses.en: And untie the knot from my tongue

verses.ar: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
verses.en: That they may understand my speech.

title: Seeking Knowledge
tag: The only thing the Prophet was told to ask for more of.
hadith: Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
Sahih Muslim 2699
opening: Allah never told His Messenger to ask for more wealth or more power. He told him to ask for more knowledge.
verse: And say: my Lord, increase me in knowledge. And: are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only people of understanding take heed. Knowledge raises a person, but only when it leads to understanding and action.
scholars: Imam al-Shafi'i wrote in a famous verse that he complained to his teacher Waki' about his weak memory, and Waki' advised him to leave sins, for knowledge is a light, and the light of Allah is not given to a sinner. Ibn Jama'ah and other scholars of learning stressed that the student must purify his intention, respect his teachers, and act on what he learns, otherwise knowledge becomes a proof against him.
modern: Carol Dweck showed that people who believe their abilities can grow learn faster and achieve more. Peter Drucker said the most important skill of the knowledge worker is learning how to learn. Professional certifications, reading and mentors are all part of the path, as long as the intention is right.
nigerian: Nana Asma'u, daughter of Shehu Usman dan Fodio, was a scholar and poet who built a network of women teachers, the Yan Taru, that educated women across the Sokoto Caliphate in the nineteenth century. And the Hausa say «Ilimi gishirin zaman duniya»: knowledge is the salt of life.
practices: Recite «Rabbi zidni 'ilma» before study or reading.
Read for twenty minutes a day in one subject: faith, your profession, or language.
Teach one thing you learn each week, as teaching fixes knowledge.
reflect: What do I need to learn to fulfil my responsibilities better?
Am I acting on what I already know?
closing: My Lord, increase me in knowledge. Walk the path, and Allah will make the path to Paradise easy.

verses.ar: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا
verses.en: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

verses.ar: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيْلِ سَاجِدًا وَقَآئِمًا يَحْذَرُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُوا۟ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِۦ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
verses.en: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.

title: Provision and Halal Earning
tag: Work as if it depends on you; trust as if it depends on Allah.
hadith: If you relied on Allah as He truly deserves, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. They go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2344
No one has ever eaten better food than what he earned with his own hands.
Sahih al-Bukhari 2072
opening: Worry about money is one of the heaviest weights a person can carry. Islam does not tell you to stop working. It tells you to stop worrying, by putting effort and trust in their proper places.
verse: Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies on Allah, He is sufficient for him. And in Surah al-Jumu'ah: when the prayer is finished, disperse in the land and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Him often. Effort and remembrance together. Notice that the birds in the hadith go out. Tawakkul is not sitting still.
scholars: Ibn Ata'illah wrote in his Hikam that your striving for what has already been guaranteed to you, while neglecting what is demanded of you, is a sign that your inner sight is clouded. Provision is guaranteed; obedience is demanded. Ibn al-Qayyim explained that tawakkul has two wings: taking the means fully, and resting the heart on Allah, not on the means.
modern: Morgan Housel, in The Psychology of Money, argues that the hardest financial skill is getting the goalpost to stop moving, knowing what is enough. Islam calls this qana'ah, contentment, and pairs it with halal effort. Wealth earned cleanly and held lightly brings peace that no salary figure can.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Kowa ya ci ladan kuturu, ya yi masa aski»: whoever takes the leper's wage must shave him. If you accept payment, give full and honest work for it. That is what makes earning halal.
practices: Begin each workday with «Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'ala Allah».
Review one source of income or expense for anything doubtful, and remove it.
Give a regular charity, however small, as an act of trust.
reflect: Where does my worry about provision exceed my effort and my trust?
Am I giving full work for every wage I take?
closing: Your provision is written, and it will reach you. Go out like the birds, work honestly, and let your heart rest on Allah.

verses.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ وَأَشْهِدُوا۟ ذَوَىْ عَدْلٍ مِّنكُمْ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِ ذَٰلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مَخْرَجًا
verses.en: And when they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for [the acceptance of] Allāh. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allāh and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allāh - He will make for him a way out

verses.ar: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُۥٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمْرِهِۦ قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدْرًا
verses.en: And will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allāh - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allāh will accomplish His purpose. Allāh has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.

verses.ar: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
verses.en: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allāh, and remember Allāh often that you may succeed.

title: Raising Children
sub: Luqman's way in a digital age
tag: Protecting the fitrah when screens are always on.
hadith: Every child is born upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian.
Sahih al-Bukhari 1385, Sahih Muslim 2658
opening: Every child arrives with a clean, natural disposition, the fitrah. What happens to it depends heavily on the people around them. Today those people include strangers on screens, algorithms and influencers. Parenting has always been a trust. Now it is also a defence.
verse: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones. The command starts with yourselves: children copy far more than they listen. Then Luqman, the wise man the Qur'an honours, advises his son. He starts with the foundation: O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Later: establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient with what befalls you. Notice the tone. Every piece of advice begins with «ya bunayya», my dear son. Warmth carries the message.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim, in Tuhfat al-Mawdud, observed that most children who go astray do so because of their fathers' neglect, failing to teach them the obligations and the sunnah of the religion. He warned against both harshness and spoiling. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab is reported to have said that a man should be like a child with his family at home, playful and gentle, yet when he is needed, he is found to be a man.
modern: Jonathan Haidt, in The Anxious Generation, argues that the shift from a play-based childhood to a phone-based childhood has driven rising anxiety among young people. He recommends no smartphones before high school, no social media before sixteen, phone-free schools, and more free play. These are practical ways to guard the fitrah.
nigerian: The Yoruba say «Ọmọ tí a kò kọ́ ni yóò gbé ilé tí a kọ́ tà»: the child we fail to train is the one who will sell the house we built.
practices: Pray at least one salah a day where your children can see you.
When apart, call or video-chat at a regular time, and ask one real question.
Agree screen-free times at home, and keep them yourself too.
reflect: What are my children learning from watching me?
Which voices are shaping my children's hearts more than mine?
closing: Protect yourself and your family. Speak like Luqman, my dear son, my dear daughter, and let your example carry your words.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَّا يَعْصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
verses.en: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allāh in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.

verses.ar: وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَٰنُ لِٱبْنِهِۦ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُۥ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱلشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ
verses.en: And [mention, O Muḥammad], when Luqmān said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allāh. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice."

verses.ar: يَٰبُنَىَّ أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَٱنْهَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَكَ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ
verses.en: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] resolve.

title: Honouring Mother
tag: Three times your mother, then your father.
hadith: A man asked: who most deserves my good companionship? He said: your mother. He asked: then who? He said: your mother. Then who? Your mother. Then who? Your father.
Sahih al-Bukhari 5971, Sahih Muslim 2548
opening: After the worship of Allah, there is almost no duty the Qur'an stresses more than kindness to parents. And among the two, the Prophet, peace be upon him, named the mother three times.
verse: We have enjoined upon man care for his parents. His mother carried him, weakness upon weakness. Be grateful to Me and to your parents. And in Surah al-Isra: your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to parents. If one or both reach old age with you, do not say to them even «uff», and do not repel them, but speak to them a noble word. Lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: my Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small.
scholars: Ibn Kathir explains weakness upon weakness as the hardship of pregnancy, then birth, then nursing, each adding to the last. In al-Adab al-Mufrad, Imam al-Bukhari records that Ibn 'Umar saw a man from Yemen carrying his mother on his back around the Ka'bah. The man asked: have I repaid her? Ibn 'Umar said: not even for a single one of her labour pains.
modern: Family therapists in the structural tradition of Salvador Minuchin teach that healthy families have warm connections and clear roles across generations. A man can honour his mother fully and still protect his own household's peace. In Islam these are not competing loyalties. Birr to your mother and justice to your wife are both commands, and a wise son keeps both without setting one against the other.
nigerian: The Yoruba say «Ìyá ni wúrà, baba ni jígí»: mother is gold, father is a mirror. Gold is precious; a mirror shows you who you are.
practices: Call your mother regularly, and let her finish speaking before you answer.
Recite «Rabbir hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira» after every salah.
If your father has passed, give charity on his behalf and make du'a for him.
reflect: When did I last speak to my mother with a truly noble word?
How can I honour my mother while keeping peace in my own home?
closing: My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. Your mother is your door to Paradise. Keep it open.

verses.ar: وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ فِى عَامَيْنِ أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَيْكَ إِلَىَّ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
verses.en: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination.

verses.ar: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
verses.en: And your Lord has decreed that you worship not except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.

verses.ar: وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا
verses.en: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small."

title: Gentleness in Marriage
tag: The best of you are the best to their families.
hadith: The best of you are those who are best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family.
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3895
Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it.
Sahih Muslim 2594
opening: Many men are gentle with colleagues, patient with clients and generous with strangers, and then bring their tiredness home. The Prophet, peace be upon him, set a different measure: your goodness is judged by how you treat your own family.
verse: Among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy. Mawaddah is warm love; rahmah is mercy that remains when feelings rise and fall. And: live with them in kindness. If you dislike something about them, perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good.
scholars: Imam al-Ghazali, in the Book of Marriage in the Ihya, wrote that good character with one's wife is not only refraining from harming her, but bearing her harm patiently and being forbearing when she is upset, following the example of the Prophet. 'A'ishah reported that the Prophet would help with the work of the household, and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to pray.
modern: John Gottman, after decades of studying couples, found that stable marriages keep a ratio of about five positive interactions for every negative one. He also found that small, daily moments, turning towards your spouse when she seeks your attention, matter more than grand gestures. Distance makes this harder, so it must be done deliberately.
nigerian: The Igbo say «Egbe bere, ugo bere»: let the kite perch and let the eagle perch. A good marriage leaves room for both to thrive.
practices: Each day, give your wife one sincere word of appreciation.
When apart, send a message with no request in it, only care.
When she is upset, listen fully before explaining yourself.
reflect: Would my wife describe me as gentle?
What do I dislike that may hold good I have not seen?
closing: Affection and mercy are gifts from Allah. Guard them with gentleness, and be the best to your family, as the Prophet was.

verses.ar: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًا لِّتَسْكُنُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
verses.en: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُوا۟ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهًا وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا۟ بِبَعْضِ مَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٍ مُّبَيِّنَةٍ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِن كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًٔا وَيَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا
verses.en: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality [i.e., adultery]. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allāh makes therein much good.

title: Guarding the Heart
tag: Freedom is mastering what you want, not chasing it.
hadith: Do not follow one glance with another. The first is yours, but the second is not.
Sunan Abi Dawud 2149, Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2777
Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires.
Sahih Muslim 2822
opening: Our age sells desire on every screen. Images, offers and distractions compete for the eyes all day. Islam does not deny desire; it trains it, so that you remain its master.
verse: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. And: as for him who feared standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from its desire, Paradise will be his refuge. The verse names the method: fear of standing before Allah, and restraint of the self. The gaze is mentioned first, because the eye is the door of the heart.
scholars: Ibn al-Qayyim, in al-Jawab al-Kafi, traced how sin grows: a glance becomes a thought, the thought becomes a desire, the desire becomes a resolve, and the resolve becomes an act. It is easiest to stop at the first step. Ibn al-Qayyim also records his teacher Ibn Taymiyyah saying that the true prisoner is the one whose heart is imprisoned from his Lord, and the true captive is the one captured by his desires.
modern: Dr Anna Lembke, a Stanford psychiatrist, explains in Dopamine Nation that constant access to pleasure leaves the brain craving more while enjoying less. Her advice is deliberate abstinence and distance from triggers. Lowering the gaze is that same wisdom, given as worship.
nigerian: The Hausa ask: «Ido wa ka raina? Wanda na gani kullum». Eye, whom do you look down on? The one I see every day. The wandering eye undervalues what is already halal and close.
practices: Remove or mute accounts and apps that pull your eyes where they should not go.
When a glance falls, turn away at once and say «Astaghfirullah».
Fill idle moments with dhikr, so the eyes and heart are occupied with good.
reflect: Which door into my heart is least guarded?
What blessing close to me have I stopped appreciating?
closing: Lower the gaze, restrain the self, and the heart becomes free. Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and it is worth every one.

verses.ar: قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا۟ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا۟ فُرُوجَهُمْ ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ
verses.en: Tell the believing men to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allāh is [fully] Aware of what they do.

verses.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
verses.en: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,

verses.ar: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
verses.en: Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.

title: Getting to Yes
tag: Negotiate on interests, not positions, and know your best alternative.
source: Roger Fisher, William Ury and Bruce Patton, Getting to Yes (1981, 3rd ed. 2011); William Ury, Getting Past No (1991)
opening: In 1979 Roger Fisher and William Ury founded the Harvard Negotiation Project. Their short book, Getting to Yes, has sold millions of copies and shaped peace talks, business deals and family disputes around the world. Its method is called principled negotiation.
idea: Most people negotiate by positional bargaining: each side takes a position, argues for it, and makes grudging concessions. It is inefficient, damages relationships, and often produces poor agreements. Fisher and Ury propose four principles instead. Separate the people from the problem: be soft on the people and hard on the problem. Focus on interests, not positions: a position is what someone says they want; an interest is why they want it, and interests can often be reconciled where positions cannot. Invent options for mutual gain before deciding. And insist on objective criteria, such as market value, precedent, law or expert opinion, so that neither side has to give in to the other's will.
mechanics: Their famous illustration is two people quarrelling over an orange. They split it in half. One squeezes her half for juice and throws away the peel; the other uses the peel for baking and throws away the fruit. Had they talked about interests, each could have had all of what they needed. The second key concept is the BATNA, the best alternative to a negotiated agreement: what you will do if this negotiation fails. Your BATNA is your real source of power. Never accept a deal worse than it, and work to improve it before you sit down. Ury's sequel adds tactics for difficult counterparts: 'go to the balcony' to control your reactions, step to their side by listening, reframe their positions as problems to solve, build them a golden bridge to retreat across, and use power to educate rather than to crush.
practice: In regulatory disputes, investor complaints and partner negotiations, positions harden quickly. Asking 'what is your underlying concern?' often reveals a path that both parties can accept: a repayment schedule instead of litigation, a disclosure instead of a dispute. Objective criteria, such as the regulator's rules or the contract's terms, depersonalise the conflict. And knowing your BATNA keeps you calm.
faith: Indeed, We have given you a clear victory. This verse was revealed about the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which many companions at first saw as a humiliation. The Prophet, peace be upon him, accepted terms that looked unfavourable: returning that year without performing 'umrah, and even allowing the word 'Messenger of Allah' to be removed from the document. But he focused on the deeper interest: peace, access, and freedom to spread the message. Within two years more people entered Islam than in all the years before, and Makkah was opened without a major battle. Allah called the treaty a clear victory. Separating the people from the problem, focusing on interests, and seeing the long game, all in one event.
nigerian: Nigeria's history is full of negotiated settlements, from labour disputes to community conflicts, that failed because each side defended positions in public while the underlying interests, jobs, dignity, security, went undiscussed. The Yoruba say «Àjèjé ọwọ́ kan kò gbé ẹrù dórí»: one hand alone cannot lift a load onto the head. Agreements that last are the ones both sides help to carry.
practices: Before your next negotiation, write your interests and your guess at theirs.
Define your BATNA, and one way to improve it beforehand.
Bring one objective criterion to the table, such as a market rate, rule or precedent.
reflect: Where am I defending a position when I should be explaining an interest?
What 'Hudaybiyyah' in my life looks like a loss but may be a clear victory?
closing: Be soft on people and firm on principles. Look past positions to interests, and remember Hudaybiyyah: what looks like a concession may be a clear victory.

verses.ar: إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُّبِينًا
verses.en: Indeed, We have given you, [O Muḥammad], a clear conquest

title: Difficult Conversations
sub: Stone, Patton & Heen · Harvard Negotiation Project
tag: Every hard conversation is really three conversations.
source: Douglas Stone, Bruce Patton and Sheila Heen, Difficult Conversations: How to Discuss What Matters Most (1999, 2010)
opening: Three teachers at the Harvard Negotiation Project spent years studying the conversations people dread: telling a boss bad news, confronting a colleague, addressing tension with a spouse or parent. They discovered that these conversations share a hidden structure.
idea: Every difficult conversation contains three conversations at once. The 'what happened?' conversation: who said what, who is right, who meant what, and who is to blame. The feelings conversation: the emotions both sides are experiencing, often unspoken but leaking into everything. And the identity conversation: what this situation says about who I am. Am I competent? Am I a good person? Am I worthy of love? Most people try to have only the first conversation, arguing about facts, while the other two drive the conflict beneath the surface.
mechanics: The authors offer shifts for each. In the 'what happened' conversation, move from certainty to curiosity: each side has different information and different interpretations. Separate intention from impact: you know your intentions, but you only guess at theirs, and they feel your impact, not your intention. Replace blame with contribution: ask how each of you contributed to the situation, which is about understanding, not fault. In the feelings conversation, acknowledge feelings, yours and theirs, rather than letting them leak out as sarcasm or coldness. In the identity conversation, accept that you will make mistakes, that your intentions are mixed, and that you have contributed to the problem, so that the conversation does not shake your sense of who you are. Finally, begin from the third story: describe the difference between you as a neutral observer would, and invite them to join you in understanding it.
practice: For leaders carrying news that others do not want to hear, such as audit findings, rejected proposals or performance concerns, the third-story opening transforms the conversation. Instead of 'you have failed to submit the reports', try 'it seems we see the reporting timelines differently, and I'd like to understand how it looks from your side'. The facts remain; the defensiveness falls.
faith: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Ibn Kathir explains that the believer is to use gentle speech and the best manner, as Allah instructed Musa and Harun to speak to Pharaoh, the worst tyrant, with gentle words, so that he might remember or fear. If gentleness is commanded towards Pharaoh, it is more fitting towards a colleague, a spouse or a parent. The Prophet, peace be upon him, when correcting people publicly, often said: what is the matter with some people who do such and such, protecting the individual's dignity while addressing the problem.
nigerian: In many Nigerian families and workplaces, respect for age and rank makes direct confrontation feel impossible, so problems go underground. The three conversations framework offers a respectful middle path: you can honour the person's status in the identity conversation while still being clear in the 'what happened' conversation.
practices: Before your next hard conversation, write out all three conversations from your side and your guess at theirs.
Open with a 'third story' that both of you would accept as fair.
When you hear a complaint, say: 'tell me more about how this looked from your side', and listen fully.
reflect: Which hard conversation am I avoiding, and what identity fear is behind it?
Where have I judged someone's intention by its impact on me?
closing: Argue in the way that is best. Get curious about what happened, honour the feelings, steady your identity, and speak gently, as even Pharaoh was to be spoken to.

verses.ar: ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَجَٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
verses.en: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.

title: Thanks for the Feedback
tag: The bottleneck in feedback is not the giver. It is the receiver.
source: Douglas Stone and Sheila Heen, Thanks for the Feedback: The Science and Art of Receiving Feedback Well (2014)
opening: Organisations spend fortunes teaching managers how to give feedback. Two members of the Harvard Negotiation Project pointed out that this misses half the picture. The person with the most control over whether feedback leads to growth is the one receiving it.
idea: Stone and Heen identify three triggers that make us reject feedback. Truth triggers: the feedback seems wrong, unfair or unhelpful, so we dismiss it. Relationship triggers: our reaction is driven by who is giving it, whether we trust them, or how they treated us, so we switch the topic to them. And identity triggers: the feedback threatens our sense of who we are, and our emotional balance collapses. Each trigger is understandable, and each blocks learning. The skill is to notice the trigger and use it as a cue to slow down.
mechanics: For truth triggers, separate appreciation, coaching and evaluation: three kinds of feedback that people often confuse. Someone who wants appreciation hears coaching as criticism. Ask the giver to clarify what they mean, and look for what is right in the feedback before what is wrong. Recognise your blind spots: others can see your tone, your face and your habits better than you can. For relationship triggers, keep two conversations on separate tracks: the feedback itself, and the issue you have with the giver. For identity triggers, notice your wiring, how strongly and how long you react, and replace all-or-nothing thinking with a growth identity: 'I am someone who makes mistakes and learns from them.' Finally, you have the right to decline feedback, but do it after understanding it, not as a reflex.
practice: Senior people rarely get honest feedback, because those below them fear the consequences. The higher you rise, the more you must actively ask for it, and receive it so well that people want to give it again. A simple question works: 'what is one thing you see me doing, or failing to do, that is getting in my own way?'
faith: Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it: those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding. The verse describes the ideal receiver: listening fully, then following the best of what is said. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab is reported to have said: may Allah have mercy on a man who gifts me my faults. In Islam, honest counsel is a gift, and the one who accepts it gracefully gains the most.
nigerian: The Hausa say «Wanda bai ji bari ba, ya ji woho»: whoever does not heed 'stop!' will hear the crowd's jeers. Feedback ignored in private often returns as embarrassment in public.
practices: Ask one colleague and one family member this week: what is one thing I do that gets in my own way?
When you feel triggered, name the trigger silently: truth, relationship or identity.
Before rejecting feedback, write down what might be right about it.
reflect: Which trigger hits me hardest?
Who has stopped giving me honest feedback, and why?
closing: Listen, and follow the best of it. Feedback is a gift; receive it in a way that makes people willing to give it again.

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُۥٓ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمْ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
verses.en: Who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allāh has guided, and those are people of understanding.

title: The Principles of Influence
tag: Seven principles that move people to say yes, and how to use them honestly.
source: Robert Cialdini, Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion (1984, new and expanded edition 2021); Pre-Suasion (2016)
opening: Robert Cialdini, a social psychologist, spent three years undercover in sales trainings, fundraising operations and advertising firms to learn how professionals of persuasion get people to say yes. The principles he found are now used by governments, businesses and, unfortunately, manipulators.
idea: Cialdini identified six principles, later adding a seventh. Reciprocity: people feel obliged to return favours. Commitment and consistency: once people commit, especially in writing or publicly, they act to stay consistent. Social proof: people follow what others like them are doing. Authority: people defer to credible experts. Liking: people say yes to those they like, who are similar to them, who compliment them, and who cooperate with them. Scarcity: things become more desirable when they are rare or disappearing. And unity: people are influenced by those they see as part of their own group, sharing an identity.
mechanics: These principles work because they are usually good shortcuts. Returning favours builds societies; following experts usually saves time. Manipulators exploit them by faking the trigger: invented scarcity, fake reviews, false authority, a small gift designed to create a large obligation.
